description: Machine-readable mirror of design_rules.md. Each entry validates against design_rule.schema.json. design_rules.md is the source of truth for prose; this file is the source of truth for gene/scorer bindings the engine consumes. Development-only; never bundled.

rules.statement: Anchor every design on a single dominant hero element; demote the rest to support.
rules.explanation: The eye needs one entry point; equal-weight elements read as a pile of assets and small parts dissolve at across-the-room distance.

genes.direction: favour single-hero templates (badge, landmark, single-country grid)

exceptions: deliberate uniform grid/collage where repetition is the concept (then enforce R-FLAG-03)

validation.signal: liked 'torn-flag' reference has focalConcentration 0.85, focalHierarchy strong

rules.statement: Give every element exactly one of three tiers (hero/support/detail) with big scale jumps.
rules.explanation: Hierarchy is deliberate difference; near-equal sizes read as undesigned.

rules.statement: Use decisive scale contrast (~1.6-2x+), not timid steps.
rules.explanation: Small size differences read as mistakes, large ones as confidence; weak contrast collapses to mush at distance.
exceptions: refined monoline quiet-luxury marks use low contrast on purpose

rules.statement: Bind related parts with Gestalt (proximity/alignment/shared shape/frame) so they read as one object.
rules.explanation: The brain chunks tight aligned clusters into one logo; floating fragments look like clip-art on a shirt.

rules.statement: Anchor the design in a deliberate containing geometry and an alignment grid.
rules.explanation: A container signals intentional boundaries and gives the generator a layout skeleton; misalignment is the subconscious cheap tell.

rules.statement: Win at 200px: one readable idea, strong silhouette, high figure/ground contrast.
rules.explanation: Marketplace purchase starts at a tiny thumbnail and the chest print is first seen across a room; fine detail dies in both.
exceptions: detail-reward pieces sold via lifestyle photography

rules.statement: Compose personalised data, never just insert it; templates must reflow by data volume.
rules.explanation: The core failure of generative merch is the Mad-Libs/auto-filled smell; a 3-country and a 40-country design must each look deliberately laid out.

rules.statement: Protect generous negative space; do not fill the shirt.
rules.explanation: Empty space signals confidence and isolates the hero; edge-to-edge crowding is the fear-of-empty-space amateur tell.

rules.statement: Contain the print (~25-30cm wide, high-center; left-chest ~7-10cm).
rules.explanation: Oversized prints crowd neckline/armholes, distort on the body curve and read fast-fashion.

rules.statement: Limit the palette to 2-4 colours including the garment (hard cap 6).
rules.explanation: Limited palettes read intentional/premium (screen-print heritage); every extra colour risks a clash and a registration layer.
exceptions: genuine full-colour illustration/AOP, still one governing palette

rules.statement: Treat the garment colour as an active ink; let it show through.
rules.explanation: On apparel the background is never neutral; using the shirt as paper/shadow tone is the premium screen-print move and saves ink.

rules.statement: Guarantee luminance (figure/ground) contrast vs the garment; never rely on hue alone.
rules.explanation: Distance legibility and colour-blind/low-light viewing depend on value not hue; mid-on-mid vanishes.

rules.statement: Prefer tonal/duotone/monochrome by default; reserve full colour for concepts that need it.
rules.explanation: Restraint reads editorial; duotone unifies flag+map+type under one mood and hides print banding.

rules.statement: Allow at most one bright accent, on a small area, for a single job.
rules.explanation: An accent works because it is rare; spread everywhere it accents nothing and turns garish.
appliesWhen: any design with a bright colour

rules.statement: Commit to one temperature story (warm sunbaked or cool alpine-nautical) plus one contrast note.
rules.explanation: Temperature is read emotionally before content; random warm+cool mixing reads as default-swatch.

rules.statement: Use muted, era-coded, derived palettes; do not use literal full saturation (esp. flags).
rules.explanation: Muted/faded reads sun-aged/authentic/premium; full-spectrum RGB freedom reads digital default.

rules.statement: Prefer off-white over pure #FFF and warm near-black over pure #000.
rules.explanation: Pure white/black inks look flat/harsh/digital and maximise the dark-garment underbase halo; cream/bone/warm-black read aged-correctly.

rules.statement: Use at most two typefaces (a third only for a distinct technical role).
rules.explanation: Each face is a voice; too many read as noise and amateurism.

rules.statement: Track all-caps and small type; kern hero display by eye.
rules.explanation: Tight caps jam and hurt readability; open tracking reads engraved/premium; big display words show ugly default gaps.

rules.statement: Match case to intent: caps for badges/official, mixed/script for warmth/narrative.
rules.explanation: Caps form stable blocks that fill rings/banners and read heritage; mixed case is friendlier/editorial.

genes.direction: upper for badge, title for narrative

rules.statement: Curve type on a true arc: consistent radius, symmetric top/bottom, even spacing.
rules.explanation: Arced type is the emblem signature and where amateurs fail (wobble, mismatched radii); a clean arc reads as a crafted seal.

rules.statement: Treat type as a designed, era-coded system (condensed=expedition, slab=heritage, mono=technical).
rules.explanation: Type carries half the storytelling; a coherent pairing does the era work; default fonts do none.

rules.statement: Never use default system fonts or render garbled/pseudo text.
rules.explanation: Default fonts and broken letterforms are the #1 cheap/AI tell. The printed string is generated downstream (TitleGen), not part of the genome; only the treatment is.

rules.statement: Solve contrast with colour/value, not outline+drop-shadow+bevel type effects.
rules.explanation: Stacked type effects are the clip-art/2000s tell and cheapen premium art.

rules.statement: Distress must follow the artwork and real wear zones, not be a uniform overlay.
rules.explanation: Genuine wear is spatially correlated with the design (bold fills, edges, folds); a uniform noise overlay is design-blind — the fake-vintage tell.
exceptions: very subtle uniform paper grain (see R-TEX-05)

rules.statement: Distress by removing ink (reveal garment), not by adding dark speckle on top.
rules.explanation: Real fade/cracks are the absence of ink so gaps show shirt colour; additive dark noise reads as dirt and the cracks are the wrong colour on dark garments.

rules.statement: Keep distress subtle (erode ~5-20%); never over-distress.
rules.explanation: Beyond ~25% it reads damaged/costume-y and flips to the dated 2010s sandblasted fast-fashion look; restraint signals premium.

rules.statement: Drive all effect layers from one shared, seeded noise field.
rules.explanation: Uncorrelated random layers read as noise soup; real wear is spatially coherent across cracks/fade/mottle. Matches the named-seed-substream determinism model.

genes.direction: single coherent fBm field per design

exceptions: fine additive paper grain may be independent

rules.statement: Add a whisper of ink mottle/fibre texture (3-8%) to flat fills.
rules.explanation: Real ink on cotton is never perfectly uniform; slight mottle makes fills read as physical print, not a vector sticker.
exceptions: ultra-clean modern minimal may want true flat

rules.statement: Emulate fades with halftones, never smooth digital gradients.
rules.explanation: The halftone dot is the fingerprint of real screen-print; smooth gradients read digital and band/halo on DTG dark garments.
exceptions: elements too small to hold dots -> posterize to flat steps

rules.statement: Halftone at 35-65 LPI with a rotated screen angle (15/45/75deg, never 0/90).
rules.explanation: Coarse dots read as intentional retro texture and hold ink; axis-aligned grids read mechanical and moire against the weave; scale LPI to print size.

rules.statement: Rasterize effects at true print DPI; the smallest feature must be >= printable size.
rules.explanation: The #1 procedural-pipeline failure is grain tuned on a small preview then upscaled — highlight dots/pinholes fall below what fabric holds and clog to mud. Generate at ~300 DPI final size.

rules.statement: Respect reproduction limits: min line ~1.5pt, min text ~6-7pt, knockout text >=8pt.
rules.explanation: DTG ink spreads into the weave; hairlines break up, tiny knockout counters fill in, small type mushes; the dark-garment underbase haloes thin light detail.

genes.direction: cap so tiles stay above min feature

exceptions: light-on-light tolerates slightly finer, still no hairlines

rules.statement: Break large solid fills and avoid full-bleed on DTG.
rules.explanation: Big flats (esp. light-on-dark) show wrinkles, print-head banding and edge halo and read as a cheap decal panel; a subtle halftone/mottle hides it.
appliesWhen: fills larger than a few inches, esp. dark/heather
exceptions: screen-print tolerates large solids; small solids fine

rules.statement: Trap / slightly overlap adjacent colours; never leave hairline gaps or perfect abutments.
rules.explanation: Emulates real multi-screen registration and prevents garment-colour slivers between abutting shapes after DTG spread.

rules.statement: Export 300 DPI transparent PNG at physical print size with a clean alpha edge.
rules.explanation: A white background prints as a white rectangle; a 1px semi-transparent halo prints as a grey underbase fringe on dark shirts.
references: This is downstream of the genome but a hard studio rule.

rules.statement: All icons/motifs share one style, stroke weight, corner radius and detail level.
rules.explanation: A mismatched icon destroys the single-author gestalt; consistency is what makes marks feel like a brand not assorted downloads.
appliesWhen: any design with 2+ icons, and across a collection
exceptions: one deliberate solid hero icon amid line details

rules.statement: A single strong icon beats an illustration crowd.
rules.explanation: Simple silhouettes survive distance, wrinkle and small print and print clean in one colour; detailed scenes lose detail exactly where apparel is viewed.

genes.direction: cap motif count, prefer one hero

rules.statement: Build from flat, simplified shapes; ban photorealism, bevels and gloss.
rules.explanation: Simplification is editorial judgement (the labour amateurs skip); flat forms read authored, photoreal/bevel read template.
exceptions: halftone/duotone photo treatments (a photo converted to a graphic)

rules.statement: Country/landmark silhouettes must be recognizable and geographically accurate.
rules.explanation: Recognition (that's MY country) is the emotional payload; a distorted/wrong outline breaks the identity signal and trust. Test at thumbnail size.
exceptions: heavy stylisation only if a name/flag restores recognition

rules.statement: Mute/unify flags; never combine several at full literal saturation.
rules.explanation: Flags are engineered for maximal individual contrast; en masse they clash violently. Render as one ink, duotone, or a tamed shared palette so form carries them.
exceptions: single-flag hero (its colours are the palette, surround neutral)

rules.statement: Contain flags (flag-in-outline); never stretch a flag to a rectangle shirt front.
rules.explanation: Containment gives form and meaning; a stretched rectangle is the cheap souvenir-stand read.

rules.statement: In flag grids enforce ruthless uniformity and normalise aspect ratios.
rules.explanation: A grid's beauty is regularity; flags vary wildly (Nepal, Switzerland, Qatar) so tokenise them into identical tiles/roundels with equal gutters and unified stroke.
appliesWhen: flag grids, stamp walls, badge collections

rules.statement: Frame as a personal journey; nationalism-neutral by default (places I've been, not conquered/ranked).
rules.explanation: Flags carry political weight; ranking/aggression reads jingoistic and limits global sellability.

rules.statement: Handle disputed/sensitive flags and borders in the data layer (neutral fallbacks, curation).
rules.explanation: Contested flags/borders (Taiwan, Kosovo, Palestine, W. Sahara) are reputational landmines; a blind generator will eventually emit something harmful. A floor, not a preference.

rules.statement: Ground every design in real, specific, verifiable data (coords/dates/elevations/true outlines).
rules.explanation: Specificity converts decoration into proof-of-experience; plausible-but-wrong details are the AI/generic tell and destroy trust. Roavvy's structural edge is real user data.
exceptions: never fabricate precision — false specificity is worse than none

rules.statement: Sell the story of the journey, not the inventory of places.
rules.explanation: A list is a database; a journey (route lines, est. year, worn passport) is emotion — nostalgia, pride, gifting.
exceptions: pure collector/grid pieces where completeness is the point

rules.statement: Make every design an explicit identity claim, not decoration.
rules.explanation: Graphic tees are low-risk social beacons; a design that clearly says something flattering-yet-true about the wearer gets bought and worn.

rules.statement: Prefer understatement and insider cues over loud tourist branding.
rules.explanation: The premium/souvenir divide is largely volume; restraint creates a traveler-not-tourist in-group flex the segment pays for.

rules.statement: Use the country outline as a container/window into meaning, not a bare shape.
rules.explanation: Filling the outline (flag, texture, visited-city dots, journey line) turns the map-site cliche into a designed, meaningful object.
exceptions: a refined variable-weight single-stroke line-art outline can stand bare

rules.statement: Commit to one coherent aesthetic world per design; no style mashups.
rules.explanation: Coherence is the master signal of art direction; the classic AI/amateur failure is a mashup because each element was optimised alone. Bundle palette+type+texture+container as locked style presets.
exceptions: skilled intentional high-low mixing (unsafe to automate)

rules.statement: Emulate a physical process (timeless), not a software filter (dated).
rules.explanation: Limited palette + halftone + real wear has looked good for 60+ years; bevel/emboss, gloss gradients, chrome, lens flares, hard drop shadows and uniform grunge are filter fashions that date fast.

genes.direction: process-emulating styles; gate era-stamped effects behind explicit retro flags

appliesWhen: default aesthetic direction for the whole generator
exceptions: knowing retro/Y2K themes behind a flag

rules.statement: Default to vintage and minimalism; adopt gorpcore/streetwear as grammars not slogans; keep maximalism/Y2K hero-only.
rules.explanation: Nostalgia and restraint age slowly; label-driven trends churn.

rules.statement: Avoid oversaturated generic tropes (wanderlust script, dotted world map, airplane+arc, compass clip-art).
rules.explanation: Undifferentiated and non-personal — they fail precisely where Roavvy's moat (real data x coherent system) should win.

rules.statement: Vary designs along curated axes with vetted ranges, never raw randomness.
rules.explanation: Random knobs produce ugly outliers; 'same 3 templates' feels cheap; curated variation gives the feel of a designed collection.
exceptions: even 'surprise me' samples a vetted space

rules.statement: Provide at least three density tiers per template, chosen by data volume.
rules.explanation: One layout can't look premium from 2 to 90 countries; branching by volume separates a design system from a mail-merge. 1-3 hero outline; 4-15 badge/stamp cluster; 16+ normalised grid / count-forward.

rules.statement: Design for the marketplace thumbnail (see R-COMP-03).
rules.explanation: Purchase decisions start at a ~200px thumbnail; bold single idea and strong silhouette win the click.

rules.statement: Keep one consistent system across a series for collectibility.
rules.explanation: A visited-more series sharing palette/type/layout grammar invites repeat purchase and reads as a curated line.
